steps.text: Water the soil around {plants}. Moist soil holds warmth overnight.
Cover {plants} with frost cloth or an old sheet that reaches the ground.
Move potted plants into the garage or against the house wall.
Remove covers once it is above 40°F so plants don't overheat.
Leave damaged leaves on {first}. They shield new growth until spring.
Pause all watering. The storm will bring more than enough rain.
Stake {first} loosely and check the tallest plants first: {plants}.
Bring pots, hanging baskets and garden decor inside.
Clear drains and gutters so water leaves the beds.
Walk the yard, straighten leaning young plants and remove broken stems.
Turn the irrigation timer off on rain days. Natives prefer drying out between waterings.
If {plants} wilt in the afternoon, check the soil 2 inches down before watering.
Check {plants} closely, including the undersides of leaves.
Water at the base early in the day so leaves dry fast.
Remove spotted leaves, bag them, and don't compost them.
Take a check-in photo and ask your UF/IFAS Extension office.
